matching: Each form: items 1-2 kinship gap-fill from a definition (parent's sibling / sibling's child style), 3-4 choice between gender pairs; EC = Arabic-L1 vowel spelling slip on a kin word in a natural sentence; FP = name a named family member in one sentence; transfer = read a short family tree description and name the relation. All words EVP A1, prompts 8-14 words. Item order identical across forms: 1-2 controlled gap-fill, 3-4 controlled choice, 5-6 error correction, 7-8 free production (target_form_0_1_2), 9 transfer. Review round 1: slots 5-6 now contain a wrong kin word that must be replaced (uncle/aunt/cousin/grandmother/grandfather, all A1); C-4 now aunt. Review round 3: all items 7-8 use the 'VOCABULARY variant, named word' rubric (as C-7 already did), since each prompt names the kin word. Review round 4: the kin-word swaps (my mother's mother is my aunt ...) were factual absurdities, not learner errors. Slots 5-6 are now vowel slips on an A1 kin word: doughter/hasband (A), parints/brather (B), grandmather/nece (C). outcomes.json l1ErrorTypes = [spelling_vowel]. Review round 5: C-6 'nece' (niece, EVP A2) -> 'childrin' (children, A1, not used elsewhere in form C); 'niece' distractor removed from A-4. No item's answer word is shown elsewhere in its form: gap-fill definitions, slot 3-4 options and slot 7-8 named kin words use only words not keyed in that form; C-9 no longer shows 'son'. User decisions (A1-A2): vocabulary validity - each form keeps one spelling error-correction item (slot 5); slot 6 is now a meaning error (Arabic-L1 polysemy or calque on an A1 word), with exactly one correct fix and the answer word not shown elsewhere in the form.
